subject: Demo summary and proposed pilot charter — Crestbridge evaluation
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@crestbridge.com>, Sasha Kim <sasha.kim@crestbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Demo summary and proposed pilot charter — Crestbridge evaluation

Hi Alex / Sasha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo and a proposed pilot (charter + milestones) so your team can review and share with procurement. Highlights below and an attached one-page charter + checklist.

What we covered (2/3 items):
- Inference performance: typical latency at 512 tokens on the models we showed (Redwood-XL-3B quantized) — ~140ms p50 on our hosted nodes.
- Integration patterns: API examples for prefix caching and how to attach your model-agnostic request router.
- Security: VPC + KMS options for Private deployment and audit log retention windows.

Proposed pilot charter (high level):
- Goal: Validate Redwood end-to-end inference for Crestbridge document summarization pipeline with a 1-week production-like workload.
- Success criteria (suggested): 1) p95 latency <= 450ms on representative 512-token batch; 2) summary quality score >= 0.82 on your team’s 150 prompt set (we’ll run blind eval); 3) cost per 1k tokens <= target discussed (~$X, we’ll refine).
- Timeline: 3-week pilot (kickoff, run, evaluation) — see detailed timeline in attached checklist.
- Ownership: Kimberly (sales) — pilot sponsor and program lead; Ben (solutions) — integration and infra lead; Marissa (CS) — success metrics and evaluation lead; Crestbridge — technical contact (Alex) and procurement (Sasha / procurement@crestbridge.com).

Immediate next steps:
1) Confirm success criteria above or provide edits by EOD Thursday.
2) If procurement needs, Sasha — I’ve attached the one-page charter for internal review; I can loop legal/procurement for tempo after you confirm.
3) If accepted, we propose kickoff the week of Aug 10 (compact 3-week run).

Attachments: redwood-pilot-charter-v1.pdf; crestbridge-pilot-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call to finalize criteria.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | redwoodinference.com
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@crestbridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sasha Kim <sasha.kim@crestbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo summary and proposed pilot charter — Crestbridge evaluation

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few quick clarifying Qs from our side before we confirm success criteria: 

1) Quality metric: Can Redwood run the blind eval against our 150 prompts and give both average and trimmed-mean (10%) so we can understand outliers? We want to avoid one bad prompt skewing the score.
2) Data handling: For the hosted run, can you confirm whether KV/prefix cache entries are stored outside our tenancy and what the retention window is? We may need a short-term retention agreement.
3) Cost target: The $X you mentioned is fine for planning — can you provide a modeled cost example for 1M tokens/day over a 7-day window using the proposed config? Even a spreadsheet estimate is helpful.

Assignees on our side: I’ll coordinate with our infra lead for the traffic profile and Sasha will shepherd procurement.

We’re generally aligned on the scope. If you can update the charter with the above items and proposed kickoff dates, we’ll get procurement moving.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Data Products
Crestbridge Analytics

Alex — great questions, answered inline below and I’ve updated the charter (see v1 attached). Short answers first, details after.

1) Quality metric: Yes — we will run the blind eval on your 150 prompts and report average + trimmed-mean (10%) and also provide the top 5 failure prompts for context.

2) Data handling: For hosted pilot (default), KV/prefix cache is stored on Redwood-managed ephemeral storage isolated per-tenant; retention is configurable — we can set a 24-hour retention window for the pilot and delete caches on pilot completion. If you need all artifacts removed immediately after the run, we’ll include that in the charter.

3) Cost model: Attached spreadsheet contains modeled costs for the proposed config — 1M tokens/day for 7 days = estimated $Y (line-item breakout included). We’ll also include delta if you prefer the Dedicated short-term option.

Updated timeline (compressed to meet your Aug 10 kickoff ask):
- Aug 10: Kickoff (confirm test dataset + traffic profile)
- Aug 11–17: Pilot run (steady traffic; Redwood runs eval jobs)
- Aug 18–19: Analysis and joint review; handoff to procurement/legal for any next steps

Owners (confirming): Kimberly (program lead), Ben (integration lead), Marissa (quality + eval lead), Alex (Crestbridge technical lead), Sasha / procurement@crestbridge.com (procurement).

Next steps for you: please confirm the trimmed-mean acceptance approach and if the 24-hour cache retention is acceptable. Once you confirm, we’ll finalize the charter and send an internal kickoff invite.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-charter-v1.pdf; crestbridge-pilot-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — I’ve also uploaded the charter to the HubSpot company record and the shared drive (links below).

Best,
Kimberly
